security.title: Security should not depend on a single model.
security.line1: Your MCP key is scoped to your organization and can be revoked at any time from Settings.
security.line2: The deterministic scanner stays authoritative — AI reasoning explains and correlates evidence, it never overrides a security finding, and no MCP tool can weaken or override your Production Verdict.
security.line3: safe_fix only ever returns a prompt for your agent to review and apply. Nothing SequrAI does through MCP executes or commits code on your behalf.

mcpPage.title: SequrAI, inside your coding agent.
mcpPage.intro: SequrAI exposes its security intelligence as an MCP server, so Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible client can check your Production Verdict, review recent changes, and request a Safe Fix — without leaving your editor.
mcpPage.whyBody: AI coding agents make software development dramatically faster. That creates a new problem: software can reach production faster than a human can properly review it. SequrAI sits between your agent and production as the security intelligence layer before deployment.
mcpPage.authBody: SequrAI issues an organization-scoped API key (seq_live_...) or an OAuth 2.0 bearer token, generated from Settings. The key travels only in an Authorization header — it is never embedded in a URL, a config file committed to source control, or SequrAI's own client bundles.
mcpPage.capabilitiesRemoteIntro: Remote tools operate on your connected GitHub repository and persisted scan history.
mcpPage.capabilitiesLocalIntro: Local tools operate on your current workspace over a local stdio bridge, without uploading source code to SequrAI.
mcpPage.workflowLine: "Review my project" → SequrAI runs a fresh review → "Can I deploy?" → SequrAI answers from the persisted Production Verdict → "Fix the top blocker" → SequrAI returns a Safe Fix prompt for your agent to apply → "Review again" → verify the risk actually changed.
mcpPage.troubleshootingBody: If your agent can't reach SequrAI, confirm the Authorization header carries a current key from Settings, and that your MCP client supports the streamable HTTP transport (Claude Code and most modern clients do; Cursor uses the local stdio bridge instead).
